contentBody: **Which statement best describes a product idea?**
option.1: A wide topic such as campus life with no named user or moment
option.2: A complaint that something should be fixed, with nothing to show
option.3: A specific user, a specific problem, and a small offer you can try
option.4: A pile of extras such as payments, ratings, and a dark mode
answerExplanation: A product idea names who hurts, what goes wrong, and a small offer that can be shown. A theme, a complaint, or a feature list is not yet something you can test.

contentBody: **After a chat tool lists many candidate ideas, what is your job?**
option.1: Filter the list and pick one idea you could show without a full product
option.2: Let the model choose, because it invented a market-size ranking
option.3: Keep every idea so none of the generated options is wasted
option.4: Start with payments and maps, then look for a user later
answerExplanation: The model’s job is volume and sharper wording. You decide. A useful filter asks whether a real person has the pain now and whether a small version can be shown without a full product.

contentBody: **What three checks make up an idea stress-test?**
option.1: Logo colour, font pairing, and animation speed on the page
option.2: Investor names, office lease, and a hiring plan for year two
option.3: Admin dashboard, OTP login, and a city-wide delivery map
option.4: Target user, the painful problem, and a believable why now
answerExplanation: Stress-testing asks who the person is, what hurts in a real moment, and why the current workaround is failing now. Decoration and extra features are not the test.

option.1: Why now means the idea is valid simply because chat tools exist
option.2: Why now names why today’s workaround is starting to fail
option.3: Why now is a slogan that replaces naming a real person
option.4: Why now is the same as listing every feature the model suggested
answerExplanation: Why now is a change in the situation — more people, a broken process, a noisy group — not “because AI exists.” AI is a tool for writing the page, not the reason the pain exists.

contentBody: **A one-line value proposition should name which parts?**
option.1: Who it is for, the outcome they get, and the pain they avoid
option.2: Only adjectives such as fast, easy, modern, and seamless
option.3: A company history and the names of future investors
option.4: The programming language planned for a later full product
answerExplanation: The value line is the sentence a stranger should understand quickly. Buzzwords, history, and later technology do not replace user, job, and pain.
